analysis.title: Global Markets Daily: Framing Off-Balance-Sheet Liabilities in the AI Ecosystem
key_insights: Hyperscaler free cash flow turned negative in 3Q2026 as capex outpaced operating cash flow, which has increased the role of debt financing in the AI buildout.

Hyperscalers (Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Oracle) have issued $271B of debt year to date as of Nov 2, 2026, above GS's full-year 2026 forecast of $250B. Three bond deals totaling $41.7B were announced since Oct 29.
Some of the 2026 issuance is a pull-forward of planned 2027 supply. GS sees scope for more, but expects market access to be uneven across issuers and dependent on market tone.

GS tracks $657B of global AI-related debt issuance year to date as of Nov 2. Only 41% was issued directly by the five hyperscalers. The rest is IG project financing, leveraged-finance project financing, IG technology, leveraged-finance technology and AI-adjacent issuers such as utilities and machinery.
Hyperscaler lease obligations total $1.7T, and more than 75% relate to leases that have not yet commenced. Because of lease accounting, the uncommenced portion is not yet a balance sheet liability.

GS estimates $1.9T of non-lease unconditional purchase commitments from SEC filings, and $685B of it is scheduled for payment by year-end 2027. The figure excludes contingent commitments such as backstop obligations.

GS believes part of these off-balance-sheet liabilities is in consensus capex forecasts, but treats the fast-growing category as an additional use of cash. It expects debt financing across syndicated and private markets to play a key role in the AI buildout.
Faster near-term monetization of AI investment is the key risk to less debt issuance. Delayed monetization and growth in purchase commitments are the key risks to more debt issuance.

Rating agencies have turned more cautious since early August. Moody's said hyperscaler aggregate financial commitments rose eight-fold since 2023 to $2.8T. S&P said the margin for error in the AI funding ecosystem is narrowing.

In late October S&P lowered the outlooks on Broadcom and Meta and cited off-balance-sheet obligations: Broadcom's residual value support liabilities from AI compute contracts and Meta's higher leverage from leasing data centers.

GS thinks evidence of AI monetization by 2028 is key to limiting downward ratings pressure. Most AI issuers are rated near the top of investment grade, so even multi-notch downgrades are unlikely to restrict most firms' market access. GS sees parallels to the pharmaceutical sector's rating migration over a decade ago.

GS expects private markets to take a larger financing role as the issuance cycle extends and syndicated credit capacity is used up. Global private markets AUM is $19.2T ($17T excluding secondaries and fund of funds), with $4.6T of dry powder ($2.9T private equity, $1.6T across private credit, real estate and infrastructure).
Private markets have completed more than $225B of data center financings since early 2025, excluding GPU and chip financing. GS sees scope for acceleration.

Capex commentary this earnings season does not point to a slowdown. Meta plans to continue investing aggressively, and other hyperscalers expect higher 2027 capex. Lower-rated hyperscalers have outlined plans to reduce capital intensity, partly through more vendor financing.
Meta's SEC filing said timing is important to secure capital before competitors saturate various funding options.
earnings_insights: 3Q2026 earnings season (reported): the hyperscalers collectively reported negative free cash flow because capex spending outpaced cash flow from operations.
Meta (reported 3Q2026 commentary): plans to continue investing aggressively in its core business and AI initiatives.
One unnamed hyperscaler (reported 3Q2026 commentary) expects capex to increase significantly in 2027. Another expects to spend meaningfully more in 2027 than in 2026.

Issuer concentration and market saturation constraints as the multi-year issuance cycle extends.
Rating agency pressure from off-balance-sheet obligations, including contingent guarantees and residual value support liabilities, with less margin for error.

tension_points.bull_case: GS expects debt financing across syndicated and private markets to keep funding the AI buildout. Ratings are clustered near the top of investment grade, so even multi-notch downgrades are unlikely to restrict market access for most firms.
tension_points.bear_case: Off-balance-sheet obligations ($1.7T leases, $1.9T purchase commitments) are growing quickly. S&P cut outlooks on Broadcom and Meta and said the margin for error is narrowing.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence of AI monetization by 2028 is the key condition for easing ratings pressure. Delayed monetization and growing purchase commitments would push toward more debt issuance.
